hypothesis.text: Campaign-finance rules can make political power substantially more local, transparent, citizen-driven, and competitive without allowing government to determine which political voices may be heard.
hypothesis.central_question: Can campaign-finance rules make political power substantially more local, transparent, citizen-driven, and competitive without allowing government to determine which political voices may be heard?
hypothesis.constitutional_capitalism_test: Can we design campaign finance so that money remains capable of supporting political speech, but wealth can no longer purchase anonymity, privileged access, or disproportionate control over the political information environment?

governance.reason: Steve-directed opening of a major research track converging democracy, journalism, political influence, and civic infrastructure. Register as hypothesis only; do not promote to doctrine, principle, or claim until evidence graduates under falsifiability.

hard_distinctions.rule: Eliminating dark money is not the same thing as eliminating political spending.
hard_distinctions.target: Radical beneficial-source traceability for every dollar used materially to influence an election — not silencing speech.

hard_distinctions.rule: Locality is not a ban on out-of-state speech about local elections.
hard_distinctions.target: An Arkansas voter giving $25 should have meaningful political agency even when national organizations are spending millions.
OpenFEC concentration and independent-expenditure reporting can deepen disclosure evidence; CC-CLAIM-003 remains Not Enough Evidence until causal capture is established.
Design tracks and empirical questions only until Supports / Qualifies / Contradicts verdicts graduate under evidence.
OpenFEC locality metrics measure disclosed contributor geography only.
Locality measures describe structure; they do not imply illegitimacy.
Size buckets are disclosure structure, not a corruption finding.
Schedule E discloses spender-layer IE activity, not coordination.

openfec_locality_probe.verdict: Partially feasible for federal contributor-state locality, size buckets, totals, and spender-layer IE; beneficial-source transparency NOT OBSERVABLE from OpenFEC alone; state/local elections out of OpenFEC scope.
openfec_locality_probe.destination_universe: Arkansas statewide, legislative, county, municipal, school-board, and other local elections
openfec_locality_probe.governing_question: Do the people governed by an election retain meaningful influence over that election's political economy?

design_target_beneficial_source_transpar.not_sufficient: Paid for by Americans for Better Arkansas alone
design_target_beneficial_source_transpar.note: Current federal independent-expenditure reporting and disclaimers are necessary but not the complete beneficial-source transparency this research describes.

legal_environment.note: Research cannot stop at Citizens United. The constitutional environment continues to move.
legal_environment.fec_note_2026_06_30: FEC states that on June 30, 2026, the Supreme Court held that federal limits on coordinated political-party expenditures violate the First Amendment.

comparative_amendment_study_only.rule: Belongs in Track B comparative legal research. Do not adopt automatically.

track_a.title: Reforms possible under existing First Amendment doctrine
focus: free or low-cost public communication infrastructure
candidate access to debates and forums

track_b.title: Constitutional architecture if current doctrine prevents the democratic system research concludes is necessary
focus: comparative constitutional amendments and state experiments
viewpoint-neutral limits on election fundraising/spending as research objects
public campaign-finance systems that preserve freedom of the press
failure modes of government-selected political speech

unintended_consequence_questions: Does outside money overwhelmingly distort some races but not others?
Do effects differ between federal, state, and local races?
Does small-donor matching increase participation but also ideological polarization?
Do strict limits protect incumbents by raising challenger discovery costs?
Does disclosure chill participation at low contribution levels?
Would reducing campaign spending without a local information economy benefit incumbents and wealthy self-funders?

journalism_convergence.rule: Campaign-finance reform must be studied alongside the local information economy.
journalism_convergence.proposition: If local elections are to become more citizen-driven, campaigns need a local information economy; otherwise reducing spending can perversely help incumbents and wealthy candidates who can already become known.
journalism_convergence.government_must_not: Decide what the newspaper says or which candidate deserves attention.
journalism_convergence.civic_system_may: Make it dramatically cheaper for citizens to learn who is running, who funded them, what they believe, what the office controls, and what incumbents have done.

civic_commons_convergence.rule: Local democratic finance instrumentation studies whether the people governed retain influence over an election's political economy; Distributed Civic Commons studies the relational culture that makes that influence usable day to day.
civic_commons_convergence.hard_boundary_shared: Political rights must never depend on participation
